why: The A-v1 upper-bound analysis (pickup/a1_budget_reachability_bound_root_v1) shows a valid bound 801 above the strongest recorded control, localised to a budget-selection effect: the controls serve 72/56/26 percent of temperature classes 0/1/2 even though the value per unit of pre-cooling energy is 9.52/6.35/4.65 per unit, i.e. they spend the energy budget on the worst class and leave cheap classes unserved. No existing registered control performs budget reservation over time.
question: Does an admission rule that reserves energy budget for later cheap-to-cool orders beat the strongest recorded control on the same frozen days?

candidate_rule.accept_condition: accept order i only if e_lower(i) <= B_remaining - reserve_for_future(clock, history), where reserve_for_future uses the frozen training history's revealed-order rate per time bucket and the per-class e_lower distribution
candidate_rule.ties: break by descending revenue per unit e_lower, then by ascending reveal time, then by ascending order id
candidate_rule.routing: unchanged: the frozen SaaReplanner / registry downstream, same K=10, same 10 s budget, same contract

controls_for_paired_comparison: the recorded per-day rows of uncond_hist, cond_hist and explicit_feat from C-VRP_Cold-chainVehicleRoutingProblem/results/a1_c1rr2_reveal_40/gate.json for the same day indices
the same frozen gate dataset identity: data_sha256 8767a03d787c0e0fcad112b4888edf46db44c55e9b50b9705bfc5830f4fb378d

panel.days: the first 5 day indices (0..4) of the frozen gate seed 20260926
panel.day_count_rationale: one day of one arm took about 570-690 s in the recorded batch with 9 workers; five days on one core is the largest panel that fits a bounded single-stage run

decision_rule_declared_before_execution.primary: paired per-day difference (candidate - explicit_feat) on utility, reported with all five day values and their mean
decision_rule_declared_before_execution.positive_lead: mean paired difference > 0 with all five days reported; this is a lead only, not a gain claim
decision_rule_declared_before_execution.extend_condition: if and only if the five-day lead is positive, extend to the full 40 frozen days in a separate pre-registered stage before any gain language
decision_rule_declared_before_execution.null_result_handling: if the lead is not positive, record the rule as dominated and do not extend; the upper-bound gap is then attributed to joint time-window and fleet coupling rather than to budget reservation, and the next step becomes the joint-coupling relaxation named in the bound addendum

forbidden: changing scenario_saa.py, run_a1_step2_gate.py or any frozen contract module in place
claiming a stable gain from a five-day panel
selecting the panel or the tie-break by observed outcome
required_before_run: build the rule as a new module in its own root (subclass, no in-place edit of frozen sources)
register that root with source hashes and the rule constants
verify the frozen dataset and contract identity inside the stage
separate production and audit processes, audit re-deriving the paired differences and the rule arithmetic
